catalog_description: Invoices billed to clients for a legal matter, built from time entries, disbursements, and retainer drawdowns.
Documented patient-provider visits with date, type, chief complaint, vitals, diagnosis and procedure codes, and attending clinician.
Requests from clinical staff to repair, configure, train on, or investigate medical devices, routed to the clinical-engineering team.
Provider documentation of patient encounters, including progress notes, nurse notes, and discharge summaries.
Provider orders for tests, medications, therapies, or procedures, with order type, priority, target facility, and results.
Managed cloud databases, warehouses, datasets, or clusters that hold structured data, tracked for security posture.
Cloud object-storage buckets or containers holding unstructured data, tracked for security posture.
Groupings of worker nodes in a cluster, with instance size, scaling config, labels, taints, and zone distribution.
cmi5 assignable units launched against a learning record store, the modern course-package standard succeeding SCORM.
Manager evaluations of a call or rep against a talk-track rubric, scoring how well the playbook was followed.
One-on-one coaching reviews, usually tied to a recorded call, with notes and follow-up actions for the rep.
Git commits on a source repository, with author, timestamp, message, parent commits, and diff summary.
Cited non-compliance with permits, building code, or regulations, with the subject, severity, fines, and remediation status.
Customer purchase orders created at checkout, tracked through fulfillment and completion.
Sellable products with name, description, SKU, pricing, and inventory references.
Physical or digital shipments tied to a fulfillment, with carrier, tracking, and delivery status. Includes returns.
Brand or channel storefronts (web store, mobile app, marketplace listing) with their catalog mapping.
Commercial real-estate leases for office, retail, or industrial space, with base rent, escalations, improvements, and renewal options.
How a transaction's commission is divided across brokerages and then internal agents, used by accounting and tax reporting.
Imported market salary data for a job-level and geography combination, sourced from external compensation surveys.
Total-rewards package definitions per role, level, and location, covering base, bonus target, equity, and allowances.
Personalized total-rewards statements showing a worker the value of their base, bonus, equity, benefits, and perks.
Role-anchored bundles of required skills and target proficiency levels, used for gap analysis and internal matching.
Tracked pieces of competitor or market intelligence, with their source, relevance, and disposition.
Profiles of tracked competitors covering positioning, pricing, strengths, and weaknesses.
Mandatory training assignments tied to a regulation, role, location, or hire event, with due dates and escalation policy.
Regulator-facing audit records of who completed which training, when, with version and evidence references.
Safeguards or actions designed to reduce risk, with control type, scope, owner, and test frequency.
Artifacts proving an obligation was met, such as audit reports, assessment results, attestations, or log exports.
Requirements imposed by a regulation or internal policy that must be fulfilled and tracked.
Formal governance directives such as acceptable-use, data-protection, or anti-corruption policies, with version, scope, and owner.
Reference table of statutes a tenant is subject to, with jurisdiction, citation, and retention period; each tenant activates its applicable subset.
Identified threats to organizational objectives, with likelihood, impact, inherent and residual severity, and owner.
Campaigns that bundle compliance training assignments by audience and due date, such as an annual code-of-conduct cycle.
Canonical records of IT things under management: servers, containers, applications, services, network devices, databases, and cloud resources.
Conflict-of-interest checks for a proposed new client, with matches across existing matters and parties and the resolution.
Source intranet platforms under governance, with platform type, base URL, authentication, crawl schedule, and status.
Lawful-basis and opt-in or opt-out state governing whether a contact's data may be processed and activated.
Unified contact-center customer identities reconciling phone numbers, emails, and customer IDs across channels.
Image repositories scoped to a cluster, with registry policies, pull secrets, and image scanning.
Container workload definitions such as deployments and jobs, with replica counts, restart policy, and scheduling rules.
Per-worker records that a mandatory broadcast or piece of content was read and acknowledged, used as read-receipt proof.
Inventory and quality assessments of web content, with page counts, health scores, staleness, and orphaned pages.
Curated groupings of enablement content organized by stage, persona, or play.
Reusable composable blocks such as heroes, calls to action, text, images, and forms used to build pages.
Binary files paired with metadata, the core records of an enterprise content management library.
Append-only events capturing when content is opened, shared, or tied to a deal, with the buyer's contact identity.
Individual structured content records conforming to a content type, served through a delivery API to any channel.
Isolated working copies of content such as dev, staging, or production, used to test content changes safely before promoting.
Editorial calendar and governance rules for retiring or refreshing content, with review dates, owners, and sunset dates.
Locales configured within a content environment, including fallback chain and default flag, driving field-level localization.
Scheduled batches of content changes published together to coordinate go-lives across many entries.
Multichannel content-syndication programs that deliver gated content to target accounts.
Schema definitions for a class of content entries, specifying fields, references, validation, and locale settings.
Supplier invoices for contingent labor, computed from approved timesheets and rate cards, then routed for matching and payment.
Timesheets from contingent workers against a work order, with approved hours, expenses, and project codes.
Non-employee resources such as contractors, agency staff, consultants, and interns, with supplier, role, rate, and end date.
Continuing education credit definitions, with credit hours, accrediting body, and eligible courses.
Formal changes to the terms of an executed contract, each tracked with its own approval and signature trail.
Reusable clause library with preferred and fallback language for terms like indemnification, IP, termination, and payment.
External parties to a contract, held separately because a counterparty may not be a CRM account or supplier and may sign many contracts.
Draft contracts handed off from an approved quote, the precursor to a signed contract.
Date-driven checkpoints in a contract, such as a delivery or review date, distinct from a deliverable obligation.
Structured threads of negotiation rounds and counterparty exchanges on a contract.
Specific commitments extracted from a contract, such as performance, payment, delivery, or reporting, each with an owner and due date.
Records of a single renewal of an existing contract, capturing the renewed term, pricing, and outcome.
Structured assessments of the legal or commercial risk in a contract or clause, produced during review.
Pre-approved contract templates such as NDAs, MSAs, and SOWs, assembled from the clause library to author new contracts.
Contractor and third-party safety prequalification records, with criteria, status, and ties to site access and permits.
Test results verifying a control's operating effectiveness, with tester, scope, result, evidence, and remediation status.
An auditor's view of testing a control: what was tested, how, sample size, exceptions found, and evidence references.
Controlled-substance receipt, dispensing, and disposal records required by the DEA, with drug, schedule, quantity, and reconciliation.
Commitments and follow-ups extracted from a conversation, tracked from open to done to confirm post-call execution.
Branching dialog graphs that orchestrate a conversational journey.
AI-extracted insights from calls, emails, and meetings, including competitor mentions, sentiment shifts, commitments, and risk signals.
Topic mentions extracted from a recorded conversation, such as competitor references, pricing, and objections, each tagged to a transcript span.
Turn-by-turn records of bot or AI-assistant conversations, with utterances, intents, confidence scores, and escalation events.
Corporate card issuance and control records, governing limits and spending controls.
Issued corporate cards, with issuer, last four, cardholder, status, and spending controls, feeding the card transaction stream.
Corrective or preventive actions arising from an incident, inspection, or audit, with owner, due date, and effectiveness verification.
Organizational units for cost allocation, with code, manager, hierarchy, and currency, driving variance and departmental reporting.
Promotion codes and campaign offers such as discounts, BOGO, or free shipping, applied to a cart or order.
Quiz or exam definitions tied to a course or lesson, with passing score and attempt policy.
Scoped catalog views surfacing a subset of courses to a specific audience, branch, or domain.
Hierarchical taxonomy for browsing and reporting on the course catalog.
Terminal completion records per learner per course version, marking the course as finished.
Forum-style discussion threads attached to a course or lesson, supporting collaborative learning.
Per-learner per-course records tracking assigned and due dates, attempts, status, and score.
Units within a course that group related lessons, supporting completion tracking below course level.
Scheduled instances of a course, with date range, location, capacity, language, and delivery mode.
Numeric ratings per learner per course, feeding aggregate analytics.
Handouts, supplementary materials, and pre-reads attached to a course offering or session.
Learner-authored qualitative reviews of a course written after completion.
Individual sessions within a multi-day offering, with per-session attendance and instructor assignment.
Free-form tags alongside categories that support faceted search of courses.
Versioned snapshots of a course's content, required to record which version each learner completed for compliance.
Learning units such as e-learning modules, videos, live sessions, or blended programs, with format, duration, and prerequisites.
Cow health incidents such as mastitis or lameness, with treatment, withdrawal period, and recovery status.
